nodes.proposition: Experiment Super Saturated is reported by multiple accounts as leaving skin hydrated or very hydrated, with formula/version unknown and conditions varying by account.
support: A04: author reports Super Saturated was lightweight, refreshing, fast drying, very hydrating, and did not leave pores feeling clogged.
A08: author reports Super Saturated left skin very hydrated when paired with tretinoin and other actives.
adjacent: A03: author still uses Super Saturated despite finding it stickier than Regimen Lab Wave Serum, because they believe it has a little more glycerin; this is continued use, not a hydration outcome.
A09: author reports Avant Guard locks in hydration from Super Saturated, but outcome allocation is joint-use and not separable.
conditions: A08 condition: used with tretinoin and other actives.
A04 context: suitable before makeup; no formula version supplied.
limitations: No objective hydration measurement.
No causal claim about ingredients, tretinoin compatibility, irritation prevention, or repurchase.
A09 is adjacent only because its hydration report is explicitly non-separable between Avant Guard and Super Saturated.

nodes.proposition: Experiment Buffer Jelly is reported by multiple accounts as a nighttime or final-step product associated with waking with glowy/glowing skin, and both accounts describe a small amount as sufficient.
support: A04: author bought Buffer Jelly seeking more nighttime hydration/repair, initially worried about thick/oily appearance, then woke with glowy, clean skin and says a tiny amount is needed.
A10: author reports Buffer Jelly locks in hydrating products, a little goes far, and they wake with glowing skin when used at night as the final routine step.
conditions: A10 condition: final nighttime step over hydrating products.
A04 condition: nighttime hydration/repair context; exact final-step routine not stated.
limitations: Hydration/repair motive in A04 is not proof of repaired barrier.
No measured skin effect or purchase event inferred for A10.
No formula version supplied.

nodes.proposition: Experiment Avant Guard has reported fit limitations around cheeks/nose or nose area in accounts describing smaller facial/head fit, while other use outcomes coexist.
support: A05: author reports an almost perfect fit except cheeks/nose, and easy cleaning.
A09: author reports fit is not the best on a very small head, especially the nose, causing a one-star deduction.
adjacent: A05: reusable-mask discovery through a TikTok creator led to immediate checkout in a sustainability context; mask possession motivates use of other hydrating/moisturizing products.
A09: author reports Avant Guard locks in hydration from Super Saturated in joint use.
conditions: A05 condition: fit issue localized to cheeks/nose.
limitations: No generalized fit prevalence claim.
A05's barrier-repair statement belongs to other products, not Avant Guard independently.
No shade preference inferred from metadata.

nodes.proposition: Experiment Softwear has a material mixed neighborhood: one account reports recommendation-driven cart readdition without use, while another reports months of liking and stock-up followed by author-attributed perioral dermatitis flare on rechallenge and a qualified recommendation warning sensitive lips.
support: A01: author put Softwear back in their cart because of the parent recommendation; this is recommendation response, not purchase or use outcome.

A11: author loved Softwear for months, called it best balm, liked thick texture/sheen, stocked up, then reports perioral dermatitis and a worse flare within 24 hours on rechallenge after recovery, attributing it to Softwear; still recommends trying at reasonable price with warning.
opposition: A11: adverse reaction report includes perioral dermatitis, rough tiny bumps, prescribed steroid cream, and worse rechallenge flare within 24 hours.
adjacent: A11: daily rubbing/brushing of dead skin was tentatively interpreted by the author as the balm working; preserve as author interpretation, not verified exfoliation.
A01: parent testimony recommends Softwear, compares Eadem, reports sensitive skin and backups, but parent is context only and not a supplied account.
conditions: A01 condition: Softwear subject resolved from parent context; no completed purchase or first-use evidence.
A11 condition: adverse rechallenge after treatment/recovery; recommendation is qualified by price and sensitive-lips warning.
limitations: This node is retained as an opposed neighborhood, not as shared experience corroboration.
Parent context is not counted as another account.
Author-attributed causation is not clinical causation.
No formula version supplied and no count of purchase occasions inferred from stock-up.

meanings: Removed Softwear from FF cart, then readded it because of parent recommendation; no completed purchase and no use result.
Crusty lips and wallet complaint are current context/humor; thanks to balm is anticipatory.
limitations: Softwear resolves from parent context; parent testimony is not this account's experience.

meanings: Likes Regimen Lab Wave Serum and finds it less sticky than Experiment Super Saturated.
Still uses Experiment Super Saturated despite relative stickiness because author thinks it has a little more glycerin.
limitations: Comparison is texture/stickiness, not hydration superiority or switching.

Parent Level Serum purchase and repurchase intention are another actor's testimony.

meanings: Super Saturated: sister introduced brand through it; author loved it, ordered their own, and reports lightweight, refreshing, fast-drying, very hydrating use without clogged-pore feeling and suitable before makeup.
Buffer Jelly: bought for more nighttime hydration/repair; initial thick/oily appearance concern, then woke with glowy clean skin and needed a tiny amount.
Face wash: immediate purchase; reports no more breakouts, makeup removed with one dollop without separate remover, and hydrated skin.
Mesh moisturizer: bought immediately at launch; no use outcome.
Brand: colorful counter presence, quirky/delightful impression, and scientist appreciation.
limitations: Chronology does not prove one benefit caused later purchases.
Product-page title does not make all clauses Super Saturated claims.
Refill label does not establish repurchase.
Survey context is not a condition on every benefit.

Reports use, almost perfect fit except cheeks/nose, and easy cleaning.

limitations: Barrier-repair statement refers to other products, not the mask independently.

Small acid-lime metadata variant does not support shade preference.

meanings: Influencer recommended Softwear; author loved it for months, called it best balm, liked thick texture/sheen despite lip-rubbing resistance, and stocked up with three unopened tubes remaining.
